## Acceptance criteria

REQ-01 is substantially implemented through generated `command_exit_codes` and [exit-codes.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/exit-codes.md:1). REQ-02 and REQ-03 are not met; see findings.

## Architecture and separation of concerns

No new domain/storage boundary violations found. The schema renderer is appropriately isolated in [schema.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/schema.rs:889).

## Functional paradigm

No blocking functional-style concerns in the reviewed change.

## Correctness and invariants

The projection contains an inaccurate `serve` mapping and is not comprehensively bound to runtime direct exits.

## Safety

No unsafe code introduced. PID safety is not relevant to this change.

## Testing

The succeeded `cargo-ci` gate records `fmt`, `clippy`, and `3606 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored`; I did not rerun tests. `./scripts/jit-validate.sh` passed. The new tests cover only two of the many exception rows, leaving the claimed runtime verification incomplete.

## Error handling

No new blocking error-handling concern beyond the undocumented/pass-through exit-code mismatch.

## CLI contract

No new command was added; JSON support is unaffected.

## Documentation

The generated reference is discoverable, but [cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:1800) and [cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:2994) retain hand-maintained command-specific exit-code descriptions.

## JIT issue management

The prerequisite `6d82de03` is done. There is no prior run history to remediate. Repository validation passed.

1. **F1 — `serve` is documented as exit code 10 despite passing through arbitrary child exit codes.** [schema.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/schema.rs:879) emits only a `serve`/`10` row, while runtime directly exits with `status.code().unwrap_or(1)` in [main.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/main.rs:6529). A child exit of 1, 42, or another value is neither represented by the generated taxonomy nor accurately described as code 10. This fails REQ-01’s command-specific mapping requirement.

2. **F2 — The claimed mechanical verification does not verify the projection against all runtime dispatch outcomes.** [schema.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/schema.rs:704) says every direct-exit exception is verified, but the new integration test exercises only `validate`/4 and `gate status-all`/4 at [command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/tests/command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs:61) and [command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/tests/command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs:90). The other hand-authored exception rows—including `serve`, gate evaluation, config validation, document validation, invariant check, and preset application—can drift without a test failure. This fails hard REQ-02.

3. **F3 — Command documentation still hand-copies command-specific exit-code mappings instead of consuming the generated surface.** [cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:1800) manually specifies `gate preset apply` outcomes, [cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:2198) manually specifies `doc check-links`, and [cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:2994) manually specifies `config validate`. These duplicate rows represented by the new projection and violate hard REQ-03.

Total findings: 3
